newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate inches up at close, quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate inches up at close, quiet trade.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed up 10 basis points at 28.30 percent after a quiet session, traders said.
"It was a very calm session, with light dealing. We're now in the holiday season where no one wants to trade until the new year," a trader said.
Other traders said the session was calm due to a stable peso. Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed virtually flat, just 0.05 of a centavo firmer at 7.8580/7.8630.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed down 60 basis points at 29.30 percent.
The central bank injected 5.004 billion pesos into the system to offset liquidity shortfalls by auctioning four credits, which it assigned at between 29.85 and 29.90 percent.

Traders said dealing was also light in the term market, where rates closed above the primary yield curve. Secondary rates on 28-day pesos closed at 28.50 percent, compared to an assignment rate of 27.37 percent.
Dealers forecast credit maturities of just one billion pesos for Friday, but nonetheless expected heavy liquidity shortfalls due to some eight billion pesos in tax payments due.
